item.title: Referees will be short-staffed at least one NFL game after nationwide ground stop
item.description: Aug 20, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; The NFL shield logo on the field at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Friday’s nationwide ground stop wreaked havoc on air travel across the country, and the NFL is feeling the effects heading into Week 10. The league has been forced to shuffle its officiating crews for Sunday’s games. One game will be a little more shorthanded than the rest. The Carolina Panthers and New Orleans Saints will play without a replay official in the stadium, with those duties being handled from New York instead. Nationwide Ground Stop The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop at 3:54 p.m. ET on Friday, and airspace didn’t reopen until 8:15 p.m. ET. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the stop was caused by switches and routers becoming overloaded and going down. More than 4,700 flights were canceled on Friday, with about 700 more already canceled for Saturday. Duffy also warned that it would “take us some time to get back to capacity.” As a result, the NFL adjusted its officiating assignments so that officials would be working games within driving distance of their hometowns. That means three backup referees will be calling games on Sunday, according to Tom Pelissero of The Ringer and Netflix. Umpire Duane Heydt will referee Panthers-Saints, while umpire Barry Anderson will work Jaguars-Titans and side judge Don Willard will referee both Dolphins-Colts and Steelers-Bengals. No Replay Official for Panthers-Saints On Saturday, Pelissero reported one more change for the Panthers-Saints game. “One more officiating change for Sunday: The Saints-Panthers game won’t have a replay official in the stadium, so his duties will instead be handled by the replay center in New York, per sources,” Pelissero wrote on X . That could put a strain on the league office, especially since Panthers-Saints is one of seven games in the 1 p.m. ET window, Pro Football Talk noted. Between a backup referee and no replay official in the building, the Panthers and Saints will be playing under some unusual circumstances. Needless to say, fans will be watching the officiating closely. item.description: Last night was a disappointing loss for the Kentucky Wildcats. There’s no way around it. Things started off promising for Kentucky, as they scored on their opening drive on a 15-play, 86-yard drive that lasted more than 8 minutes. However, Kentucky’s offense struggled the remainder of the game, as the Cats would only manage 156 yards of offense the rest of the night. The defense was strong in the first half, forcing the Gators to punt on all five of their offensive possessions in the first half, as the Gators only managed to score via a safety on a controversial holding call against the Wildcats that the officials said occurred in the end zone. The second half was a different story, though, as Kentucky simply could not stop Florida QB Aaron Philo from consistently picking up yards on the ground. Philo, who entered last night’s game with 104 rushing yards on 44 carries this season, finished with 102 yards on 15 carries against Kentucky, nearly all of which came in the second half. The loss essentially knocks Kentucky out of playoff contention, as the Cats fall to 7-3 on the season. Kentucky entered last night’s game ranked 11th in the College Football Playoff rankings, and 13th in the AP Poll and Coaches Poll. After a second consecutive loss, where will Kentucky land in the new rankings? Chip Patterson from CBS Sports projects Kentucky will be ranked 17th. item.title: Wilson’s Bold Start Lifts No. 9 Indiana Past USC In Key Win
item.description: Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images No. 9 Indiana needed a spark to fix its postseason resume, and fill-in quarterback Grant Wilson delivered it in a 27-13 victory over No. 18 USC. The Hoosiers had struggled to score points or move the ball since late October, but the team looked like a complete unit on Saturday night. After taking over for the injured Josh Hoover, seventh-year player Wilson, who had not started since 2024, immediately pushed the offense to be more aggressive. Coach Curt Cignetti made the call to start Wilson on his way home from the Oct. 31 road trip against Minnesota. “He pulled me to the side while out there at practice, and he goes, ‘You’re going to go with the ones,’ and then turned around and walked away,” Wilson said of the moment he learned he was the starter per ESPN . The offense threw deep right from the opening drive. Abandoning the Safe Plan Indiana had been playing too conservatively for the last two weeks, a style that Cignetti admitted the team hated. “We’ve been kind of playing in the tent, so to speak, the last two weeks, conservative,” Cignetti said. The team immediately looked downfield, with Wilson’s first completion going for 47 yards to Shazz Preston. “We took some shots there on the first drive, kind of set the tone for the game, got them to back up a little bit, play their shell, and then we got them to switch out of it,” said Wilson per ESPN. Nine of his 17 completions gained at least 12 yards, showing that the offense was willing to take risks to win. A Boost for the Whole Team Wilson finished with 305 passing yards, two touchdowns, and one interception, leading the Hoosiers to their best win of the season. The passing game gave the offensive line a break from constant run-blocking duties, which helped the entire unit play with more confidence. Khobie Martin also helped the ground game after missing the first half of the season with an injury. Despite the win, Cignetti did not promise that Wilson would keep the starting job. “What he’s been going through is tough,” Wilson said about Hoover. “I don’t wish that on anyone. … He’s gone through so much with his shoulder. He’s a great teammate.”

item.title: Banton pushes case and bowlers sparkle for inconsistent England
item.description: Baker was making his first appearance against Australia [Getty Images] Second one-day international, Adelaide England 355-6 (50 overs): Banton 121, Cox 67, Root 62 Australia 220 all out (44.3 overs): Green 64, Renshaw 63; Atkinson 4-28 England won by 135 runs; series level at 1-1 Scorecard Tom Banton scored a century and Sonny Baker and Gus Atkinson impressed with the ball as England's wildly inconsistent one-day team hammered Australia to set up a series decider. Banton scored a fine 121 – pushing his case for selection further with a second ODI hundred – in England's 355-6. After being knocked over for 131 two days ago in Perth, England's total was their highest in one-day internationals in Australia. And then their bowlers, who failed to defend 430 against Sri Lanka last month and were undone by an improbable last-wicket partnership against Pakistan, reduced Australia to 29-4 inside seven overs and easily closed out a 135-run victory. The win ends a seven-match losing run against Australia across formats in Adelaide - and a run of six consecutive defeats by Australia in 50-over cricket away from home. But, more significantly, it corrects their course after those damaging defeats against Sri Lanka, Pakistan and Australia and offers positives amid the frustrations going into the decider on Wednesday (03:30 GMT) in Hobart. Baker a smart selection Will the real England please stand up? Before those defeats in Rawalpindi, Lahore and Perth, England had won three ODI series this year. This win only adds to the feeling they are extremely difficult to figure out. Banton was superb and, even more encouragingly, Atkinson and Baker were too. This England team has often struggled for new-ball wickets and Baker, brought in for Jamie Overton in an attempt to correct that fault, found significant swing. He took the key wicket of Australia captain Mitchell Marsh, taken high at slip by a diving Joe Root, for two. Atkinson used nip to nick off Travis Head for seven – the second match in a row he has dismissed the Australia left-hander – and also have both Cooper Connolly and Josh Inglis caught behind. Career-best figures of 4-28 are reward for good recent performance that have often gone unrewarded. England were not perfect. They dropped four catches – first Inglis and then Matt Renshaw and Cameron Green, who made 63 and 64 respectively to drag out Australia's score. But by the end, Sam Curran had taken two wickets in two balls, including bowling Jack Edwards with his moon ball, in a boost after his poor run. Green was also out stumped when the ball deflected off Jordan Cox's shin and onto the stumps and Liam Dawson took 2-41 as he was preferred again to Adil Rashid. These are the performances that suggest England can challenge at next year's World Cup, but plenty more are needed. Banton pushes case Banton's chance as opener has come courtesy of Jacob Bethell's knee injury. In nine innings, he has scored four fifties and two hundreds. The spot should now be his

item.title: Wenger decides not to challenge Fifa chief Infantino
item.description: Arsene Wenger had considered running for the Fifa presidency [Getty Images] Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger has decided not to stand against Gianni Infantino as a candidate in Fifa's presidential election. The Frenchman had been considering running for the job but sources have told BBC Sport that he has ruled himself out. Current world football chief Infantino's position was plunged into crisis by a backlash caused by his failed plan to sell commercial stakes in the World Cup to private investors. Wenger - who is Fifa's head of global development - would have had the backing of European football's governing body Uefa, which has spearheaded opposition to Infantino. On Saturday, French newspaper L'Equipe reported that Wenger was unlikely to challenge his boss. Wenger has credibility throughout the footballing world, and this will be a significant boost to Infantino as he seeks a fourth term as president. Uefa is said to still be hopeful of finding an alternative candidate before Wednesday's deadline. One influential figure in the group of stakeholders opposed to Infantino told BBC Sport the news was "a real shame". "Even if not perfect, I do think he could have galvanized many around the world," they added. Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega was the first person to put his name forward in October. Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima has also announced his intention to stand. However, sources have told BBC Sport that the 68-year-old has not yet secured the necessary five endorsements from member associations ahead of Wednesday's deadline but is "still fighting hard". Amid the fallout over FFE, Wenger, who has traditionally been loyal to Infantino, distanced himself from the aborted plot. "I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports," Wenger said at the time. "The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent Fifa that serves our game with commitment, transparency and integrity." Infantino has retained support in South America, Africa and Asia, and recently insisted he has the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of world football. FIFA has been approached for comment. item.title: Arsenal star plays through illness for national team
item.description: Arsenal star plays through illness for national team Martin Odegaard was up all night feeling unwell before Norway’s match against Wales on Saturday, but he went on to play 90 minutes anyway. Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images Norway captain Martin Odegaard hasn’t missed a minute of his country’s 2026/27 Nations League campaign so far, but there was a strong argument for him sitting out of Saturday’s game against Wales . According to Norway manager Stale Solbakken , Odegaard was up all night before the game due to illness, but he pushed to play 90 minutes anyway. “We have had a captain who has been lying around all night vomiting,” Solbakken said . “All credit to him for going the distance. We had a conversation during the break that he should just go for it from the start and let us know when the tank was empty.” Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images Odegaard’s Norway teammate Patrick Berg confirmed his manager’s claims, praising the player for being able to finish the match anyway. “I understood that Martin had a bad night,” Berg said. “It’s not exactly optimal when you’re going out and playing a football game. It’s strong of him to be able to finish. “As far as I know, the illness is only affecting one person. We can only hope that it stays that way. But it is not unusual for it to spread.” Photo by Marius Nordnes / Nordnes Foto/Getty Images For what it’s worth, the game went well. Odegaard created three chances as Norway won 3-1, ending a run of three consecutive defeats. Norway had been slipping towards relegation, but they’re now safe from automatic relegation, and they could even achieve a top-two finish and make the Nations League quarter-finals if they win their final game against Denmark . If they don’t win that match, they’ll be playing in the relegation play-offs in March. Photo by Marius Nordnes / Nordnes Foto/Getty Images

item.title: Jason Kelce reveals what he hates about Eagles that could make owner Jeffrey Lurie angry
item.description: Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Jason Kelce has a take that could make Philadelphia Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie angry. Jason Kelce spent his entire 13-year NFL career with the Philadelphia Eagles and retired as a franchise legend in 2024. Even though Kelce is no longer an active player, he always shows unwavering support for the Eagles through his ‘New Heights’ podcast. Speaking on his podcast, Kelce recently revealed what he hates about the Eagles that won’t sit well with owner Jeffrey Lurie. Jason Kelce wants Philadelphia Eagles to wear retro jerseys Kelce explained that he’s stunned that teams no longer prefer wearing retro jerseys. For the Eagles in particular, he shared his favourite retro jerseys that predate the time that Lurie has owned the franchise. “I don’t know why everybody is not wearing retro jerseys. I hate all of the new jerseys. … Kelly Green, in my opinion, should be the main jersey for the Eagles. “Technically, Midnight Green was instituted in the 90s when Jeffrey Lurie bought the team. Jeffrey would not be happy that I’m saying this, but I do like the Kelly Green more,” Kelce said. He added, “Midnight Green was better when it was Reebok-owned. There was a sheen and a shininess to it. Now that the Nike jerseys are stretchy and it’s not the same material, the Midnight Green doesn’t look anywhere near as cool.” For context, Lurie bought the Eagles in 1994, and it didn’t take long for him to end the Kelly Green jerseys, as the Midnight Green jerseys were introduced in 1996. While the Eagles have been successful in the Midnight Green jerseys, Kelce still thinks the Kelly Green ones were superior. item.title: Erling Haaland snaps back at questions over Man City charges
item.description: Erling Haaland says he is "incredibly happy" at Manchester City , insisting his focus remains on performing rather than potential sanctions against the club . City have launched an appeal having been found guilty of more than 100 breaches of the Premier League ’s financial regulations. If the verdict stands, the club could be subjected to heavy sanctions, including huge points deductions or demotion. Haaland addressed the case following Norway’s 3-1 Nations League win over Wales in Oslo on Saturday night, where he registered his 66th goal in 60 international appearances. “This is a question I struggle to answer, because it’s a legal battle between the Premier League and Manchester City,” Haaland told Norwegian broadcaster TV2. “Am I supposed to answer that? I don’t really know. It’s a difficult question to answer when I don’t know that much about it. “To be completely honest, I’m focused on trying to perform for Manchester City. A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022, and a new nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024. “I think that says everything about the matter. I’m a City player and I’m incredibly happy there.” Asked if the situation affects his City future, Haaland replied: “I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I said I signed a long-term contract in 2024. Erling Haaland says he is happy and focused on performing amid the Premier League club’s off-field issues (PA Wire) “I’d say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that. “I won’t say it myself, but look at the trophies I’ve won and how I’ve developed on and off the pitch. “I’m standing here after winning an international 3-1. Things aren’t going so well in the Premier League, but we’ll try to turn that around against Fulham (on Saturday).” City maintain they have a “comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence” to support their case, despite being found guilty by an independent commission in September. The commission’s damning findings included breaches relating to the concealment of funding worth more than £830million over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018. Haaland was asked about the case after Norway’s 3-1 Nations League victory over Wales, in which he scored his 66th goal in 60 international appearances (AP) Haaland said the period under investigation happened before he joined City, and in the interview he painstakingly pointed out each stage of his football journey during that time. He also name checked fellow Norwegian players Abdisalam Ibrahim, Martin Samuelsen, Omar Elabdellaoui and Kjetil Haug, who spent time at City during that era. Haaland said: “The investigation covered 2009-2018. I assume the answers will come. “I don’t know when. I haven’t read much about it.”

item.title: ‘Loserdom’ – U.S. soccer legends ripped for calling Pep Guardiola a bad fit to lead the USMNT
item.description: Photo by FRANCK FIFE/AFP via Getty Images The recent reports linking the United States Men’s National Team to Pep Guardiola as Mauricio Pochettino’s replacement as manager have irked two former USMNT stars. The United States have always been considered one of the sleeping giants in world soccer, as the sport has not had the cultural appeal of American football (NFL), basketball, or baseball. But success at the international level could change that for the next generation. As USMNT have recently committed to building themselves up as an international powerhouse in the sport, they’re linked with a big-money move to make Guardiola their new manager. However, it seems two recent legends heavily disagree. Landon Donovan and Tim Howard labelled jealous by fans after Pep Guardiola to USMNT take Donovan and Howard could rank as the two greatest players in the history of the USMNT, but the legends don’t think Pep would fit as the USA’s manager. Tim Howard: “He’s absolutely not the right manager for this team… Guardiola has only ever succeeded with tier-one players. People might get upset with this. We have probably tier-three players globally.” Landon Donovan: “Pep is a phenomenal manager, but this would not be right for the U.S. team. Would he be good for our 18-year-old players? I don’t know. We have good, elite players, but he’s been with the best.” Their take was ridiculed by fans of the USMNT, with many labelling them jealous, as a new era under Pep might lead to their nation-leading achievements in the sport to be forgotten. “The level of loserdom required to conclude that the winningest coach in the history of the sport wouldn’t be a “good fit” for your team is other-dimensional,” said one very angry fan . “I honestly believe these two dip—- want US soccer to continue to fail so they can continue to talk about their glory days…” said one fan calling out their potentially selfish reasons behind the take . “Best manager in the last 20 years? No, we don’t want him. Let’s bring in the Vancouver Whitecaps manager instead. Howard is the most capped goalkeeper in USMNT history, with the former Everton shot-stopper registering 42 clean sheets over 121 appearances. item.title: Atlanta Dream star scores 22 points in her first game since losing WNBA finals
item.description: Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images Izzy Borlase is quickly proving why she’s one of the brightest young talents in basketball right now. At just 22 years old, Australian guard Izzy Borlase put together a really solid rookie WNBA season with the Atlanta Dream in 2026. Playing in all 44 regular-season games, she gave Atlanta a reliable spark off the bench, averaging 4.8 points, 1.5 rebounds, and an assist in 13 minutes a night. Once the playoffs hit, her role only grew. Across the seven-game WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries, Borlase stepped up on the biggest stage, putting up 4.9 points and 2.3 rebounds a game, including a 12-point, five-rebound night in Game 3 and a huge second-half spark in Game 7. Izzy Borlase scores 22 points for Bendigo Spirit Izzy Borlase didn’t waste any time making her presence felt in her season debut for the Bendigo Spirit, helping lift the previously winless 0-5 squad to a massive 27-point over ladder-leading 5-1 Sydney. She set the tone right away, pouring in 13 points in the first half to send Bendigo into the main break up by 14. By the final buzzer, Borlase had filled up the stat sheet with 22 points, four rebounds, five assists, two steals, and a block. Before heading over to the WNBA, Borlase was already a star back home in the WNBL. She got her start with the Adelaide Lightning in 2022, quickly picking up Breakout Player and Sixth Woman of the Year honors, before joining Bendigo and taking home both the scoring title and league MVP in 2026. item.title: 'We've waited 73 years to be here' - Wales fans ecstatic after win over New Zealand
item.description: Saturday marked the first time Wales had beaten New Zealand in 73 years [Getty Images] Welsh rugby fans were "fizzing off their heads" on Saturday night after ending 73 years of hurt against New Zealand in an epic Nations Championship encounter. The match at the Principality Stadium ended 35-28 to the hosts as the All Blacks' run of 34 successive victories against Wales - dating back to 1953 - came to a juddering halt in Cardiff. Wales fans were left stunned by a result that came just a week on from having to grind out a win against Japan. Prince William, patron of the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) also congratulated the team on the win, saying it was a "fantastic result". Three times Wales led by 14 points, and for the first time in history they scored five tries against New Zealand, but ultimately it was heroic defensive work that denied the visitors. All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie made eight changes from the side that swept past Scotland in their previous Nations Championship game. But the approach backfired spectacularly after a brilliant performance sparked astonishing scenes in Cardiff . A crowd of 55,152 could scarcely believe what had unfolded, and there were scenes of wild celebration with players in tears as Wales began taking in arguably the most famous win of their 145-year Test match history. Wales now holds The Raeburn Shield - a fan-created trophy that traces match-winners in men's rugby union back to the first international rugby union match in March 1871 [Getty Images] Prince William shared a post on Instagram saying it was a "fantastic result by the Wales rugby team". "My congratulations to the players, coaches and everyone who played a part - you have given fans across Wales a day they will never forget". Celebrities and politicians were also quick to pay tribute to the team for their heroics on the field. Speaking on 5Live Breakfast on Sunday morning , First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth said: "Yesterday, meant a heck of a lot to us. "We are a pretty sporting mad nation. Rugby is very important to us as a nation. "The fixture against New Zealand is a particularly important fixture. We are a smallish country but in the rugby world, we are the biggest powers. He continued that "73 years we have failed to beat them, we have come close". "I have watched Wales come close some 20 years or so ago but sport is wonderful and awful at the same time. It became this psychological block. "Well, no more. That is it, we can go forward now with a new generation knowing that we can beat New Zealand." He said the crowd on Saturday "wasn't the biggest, but no doubt that changes". "I full expect the game next week to be a sell out." Gavin and Stacey star Jones shared her sheer delight in an Instagram video, with the actor looked visibly stunned following the incredible win over New Zealand. "This has been decades in the making. item.description: It was a banner outing for the state at the 91st New England cross country championships , which were held Saturday, Nov. 14, in Maine. It feels like every practice, every game, every press conference is being studied under a microscope. And following a rough 0-4 start to the season, many believed that newly finished ceiling was already ready to collapse. However, Antetokounmpo and his new teammates are showing the basketball world they’re going to be just fine. On Saturday night, Antetokounmpo and the Heat absolutely routed the Detroit Pistons, 137-117. After losing their first four games of the season, they have now won four straight games, the second-longest, current winning-streak in the Eastern Conference (Boston Celtics, 5). Giannis Highlights Great Team Effort Following Blowout Win And just as Antetokounmpo was required to answer questions last week on if he doubts his new team’s ability to win, now he’s able to answer questions on his team’s excellent effort. Antetokounmpo took this opportunity to make a bold statement, mixing in what appeared to be a veiled shot at the doubters from last week — who have since gone into hiding. “Just figuring out as a team, I think we just clicking better. We know each other’s spots better, and the most important thing out of all, we’re competing. Our effort is way better than the first four games,” Antetokounmpo said. The Heat now own a record of 7-6, and Antetokounmpo continues to be the superstar leader his squad needs. item.title: College Football game between Louisville and UNC ends in heated on-field brawl
item.description: Louisville Cardinals ‘ 16-14 victory over North Carolina Tar Heels ended with a heated on-field brawl as players from both college football teams clashed after the final whistle on Saturday night. The incident happened in Chapel Hill after the Cardinals secured their fifth consecutive win. Players began exchanging words during Louisville’s victory formation before pushing escalated into several physical confrontations. The tension followed a crucial defensive play by Louisville. With 58 seconds remaining, defensive back Jabari Mack intercepted a fourth-down pass from North Carolina quarterback Travis Burgess. Mack returned the ball 32 yards before sliding to secure possession. Louisville then ran out the clock to claim the two-point victory. MORE: Landry Kiffin turns heads in stunning yellow minidress for final LSU home game However, the postgame celebration soon turned into chaos. North Carolina defensive tackle Xavier Lewis and Louisville offensive lineman Johnnie Brown III continued jostling after the final kneel-down. Other players soon joined the confrontation. Several pushed and grabbed opponents, while apparent punches were thrown during multiple skirmishes across the field. Mandatory Credit: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) North Carolina head coach Bill Belichick stepped onto the field to help separate players. One confrontation also spilled into the end zone, where another group became involved.
